articleTitle: Measurement of the Electromagnetic Properties of Materials Based on A Refined Transmission-Reflection Algorithm
abstract: A refined algorithm is presented based on the traditional NRW transmission-reflection method (T/R method). According to the magnetic property of the material under test, the algorithm can get different solutions, then obtain the complex permittivity and complex permeability of magnetic material simultaneously or the complex permittivity of nonmagnetic material. It solves the half-wavelength divergence problem and the multi-roots problem which exist in the traditional NRW algorithm and overcomes the machining and assembling problem of thin samples which is required in the traditional algorithm. Tests of air and PTFE are carried out to verify unreliability of this test system and the results are consistent with true values.

articleTitle: Particularities of Polarization-Mode Dispersion in optical fiber with Wavelength Division Multiplexing during the Lightning stroke
abstract: In this paper it is considered the problem of exposure of lightning strokes upon optical fiber without metal in cable design. The wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) systems development with increasing number of carriers brought to transmission in the same transparency window some tens or hundreds waves. The polarization plane rotation during the lightning stroke will be different for each wave: the short waves rotated greater then the long waves. The long waves will have in preference the vertical polarization and the short waves will have horizontal polarization .On input of optical amplifier a packet of waves with different polarizations will appear, and it can produce problems to filters, optical insulators and amplifiers. Other result of influence of lightning there will be additional polarization-mode dispersion (PMD). PMD of such nature can produce problems under interaction with time division multiplexing (TDM) and synchronization under a high rate of transmission.

articleTitle: Transfer Impedance of SMA Receptacle as Wideband Measurement Electrode for Discharge Current from Charged Human
abstract: We have derived a transfer impedance of an SMA receptacle as a wideband measurement electrode being used for discharge currents from a charged human, and have measured its frequency characteristics from 300 kHz to 20 GHz. With a 12 GHz digital oscilloscope, measurement of discharge currents through a hand-held metal bar from a charged human was also made, and thereby the injected currents on the SMA receptacle were reconstructed from the measured transfer impedance.

articleTitle: Measurement of Discharge Currents due to Human-ESD
abstract: Using a 12-GHz digital oscilloscope, we have measured discharge currents through a fingertip or a hand-held metal bar from a charged human body with a charge voltage of 600 V, and have compared their discharge waveforms in conjunction with the corresponding discharge voltages, which were derived from our previously proposed equivalent circuit model.

articleTitle: Transmission Characteristic Analysis for UWB Body Area Communications
abstract: With the rapid progress of electronic and information technology, an expectation for the realization of body area network (BAN) by means of ultra wide band (UWB) techniques has risen. The objective of this study is to analyze the transmission characteristics by using a high-precision human body model in order to eliminate the influence of antenna structures on channel modeling. A frequency-dependent finite difference time domain ((FD)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>TD) method and a Matlab-based curve-fitting tool are employed for the modeling of channel characteristics. Based on the numerical results, the path loss and power delay profile are derived statistically.

Author Keywords: frequency-dependent finite difference time domain ((FD)2TD) method

articleTitle: On the Mutual Coupling of the Finite Microstrip Antenna Arrays
abstract: Mutual coupling between radiation frequency (RF) components, antenna elements in a microstrip antenna array or between two microstrip antenna arrays is a potential source of the performance degradation. The degradation includes the impedance mismatching, the increased side-lobe level, the deviation of the radiation pattern from the desired one, and the decrease of gain due to the excitation of the surface wave. In the application of continuous wave radar, when the transmitting antenna and the receiving antenna are placed closely side by side, the transmitting energy may even blockade the receiver. In the application of adaptive nulling arrays, the mutual coupling will result in the serious degradation of the adaptive nulling performance. The mutual coupling is also important to the issues of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) when a lot of RF systems work simultaneously in a limited space, especially to the signal integrality (SI) design. The mechanism of the mutual coupling is quite complicated which involves both the near field and the far field couplings. In dealing with these problems, the full wave analysis is indispensable. In the meantime, in the analysis or optimization design, the frequency response should be taken into account as well. In this paper, the effective frequency dependent full wave analysis will be introduced. Examples of mutual coupling reduction are given that involve the mutual coupling reduction between two microstrip antenna arrays and the mutual coupling reduction between microstrip antenna elements,. In addition, the mutual coupling effect on the performances of some antenna arrays will be briefly addressed.

articleTitle: Analysis and Test of EM Shielding for Low-Frequency Magnetic Field
abstract: Electromagnetic shielding is the technique that reduces and prevents coupling of undesired radiated electromagnetic energy into equipment, so as to enable it to operate compatibly in its electromagnetic environment. Usually, the frequency considered for electromagnetic shielding design is above 10 kHz, but the lower frequency for some special demand is 50 Hz or even 0.01 Hz sometimes. This paper mainly studies the shielding design for low-frequency magnetic field, and the shielding effectiveness of single shielding and multimedia shielding are discussed separately. Moreover, the shielding effectiveness of a steel shielding enclosure and two different shielding doors for low-frequency magnetic fields in the near zone is measured.

articleTitle: Analysis of Shielding Effectiveness of Rectangular Cavity with Improved Aperture Model
abstract: This article first introduces the improved theory of transmission line method (TLM), which is used to analyze shielding effectiveness of rectangular enclosure with improved aperture model. The calculations show that the contours of TML shielding efficiency is in agreement with the that of FDTD calculation. Then we expand the fundamental formulas to deal with the cases of multi-holes, and arbitrary angle of polarization. Simulation results indicate that: when the frequency is under resonant frequency, the closer to the enclosure, the more the coupling energy is; resonance appears between the aperture and the enclosure, which results in low even negative shielding effectiveness in the metal shell; shielding effectiveness increases when polarization angle increases, and shielding of low frequency is better than that of high frequency; for the same areas, shielding effectiveness of a single hole is worse than that of multi-one. Suggestions to the shielding are proposed.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility of UHF-RFID to GSM
abstract: Global scale article track and information share can be achieved by combining RFID technology with global network, i.e. mobile communication network. However, the power transmitted by RFID reader or responded by RFID tags would probably cause interference to the communication link between the phone and base station. This paper presents in what, condition a RFID system would not cause performance degradation to GSM network while the RFID system is integrated into the GSM network.

articleTitle: Simulation of Electromagnetic Induction on DC Transmission Lines from Parallel AC Transmission Lines
abstract: When HVDC and HVAC transmission lines are set along the same right of way, electromagnetic coupling will be generated. Based upon the EMTDC software, the electromagnetic induction between DC and AC transmission lines is researched. The equivalent model of converter station is given at steady state and its validity is testified. At the same time, the parameters influencing the electromagnetic induction are analyzed and some useful conclusions are drawn.

articleTitle: Analysis on Shielding Effectiveness of Aperture Arrays with Different Spacing
abstract: The shielding effectiveness of aperture arrays with different shapes is calculated and analyzed. The influence of the spaces between the adjacent apertures is analyzed. The results show that: when the spaces between the adjacent apertures is larger, the coupling of the adjacent apertures can been neglected , the contours of shielding efficiency of the transmission line method agrees with that of TML method; When the spaces between the adjacent apertures is smaller , the coupling of the adjacent apertures can be strong , the closer the adjacent apertures is, the more the field is coupled into the shielding enclosure, and the shielding efficiency is getting worse, especially in low frequency. But the shielding efficiency contours does not change much. In the same condition the shielding effectiveness of round arrays is minimum. According to the calculation result, suggestions to the shielding are proposed.

articleTitle: Adaptive Frequency Selective Surface with ring slot units
abstract: Single layer and double layer adaptive FSS with ring slot units has been investigated in this paper. Ring slot FSS acts like band-pass filter. It can be used in antenna radomes. Lumped-element devices are loaded on the periodic units. Resonant frequency of the FSS depending on the lumped-element' capacitance could shift in a specified frequency band. The bandwidth of the FSS with reflection loss below -10 dB can get to 10 GHz.

articleTitle: 3 High-order Mode Transmission Line Model of Enclosure with Off-center Aperture
abstract: An analytical formula has been developed for shielding effectiveness of rectangular enclosure with off-center aperture. The presented formula has been extended to include high-order modes and loss of enclosure. It is necessary to take modes higher than TE10 into account when aperture locates off-center.

articleTitle: A Novel Compact Defected Ground Structure with Cross-Finger Gap
abstract: In this paper, a novel compact defected ground structure (DGS) with cross-finger gap was proposed. Comparing to conventional structure, the new structure increases the equivalent gap capacitance by adopting the cross-finger shape, instead of the conventional direct edge shape. Due to the DGS stopband theory, the higher equivalent capacitance means the lower stopband. Consequently, for the same stopband, the DGS wi th cross-finger gap has the more compact size. This novel compact DGS was simulated and verified. The compact size may reduce the back-radiation from the etched DGS in the ground.

articleTitle: Shielding effectiveness of an enclosure with a dielectric-backed aperture using slotline method
abstract: A new analytical formulation is presented for the shielding effectiveness of an enclosure with a dielectric-backed aperture. The shielding effectiveness may be calculated as a function of frequency, dielectric constant, and position within the enclosure. And, a formulation has been developed for the shielding effectiveness of the structure where the one side of dielectric is partially backed by conductor.

articleTitle: Time Domain Measurement of Voltage Rise Time and Current Rise Time Due to Low Voltage ESD using 12GHz Experimental System
abstract: Voltage rise time and current rise time due to small gap discharge as the low voltage ESD was investigated in time domain. The measurement system was improved on the band width from 6 GHz to 12 GHz using the coaxial electrode system. Also, the sensing system was changed from the coupled transmission lines to an E-field sensor and a H-field sensor. The insertion loss of the experimental system was within about -3 dB in frequency range below 12 GHz. As a consequence of the experiment using the system, voltage and current rise time of transition duration were shown 32 ps or less. The rise times were changed in configuration of electrodes, source polarity and discharging voltage. Besides, breakdown field was examined to corroborate the very fast transition durations of about 32 ps. The breakdown field was very high of about 8times10 V/m in low voltage discharging of below 330 V.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Conducted Interfering Mechanism within SVC-based substations
abstract: In this paper, a simulation model is established to investigate on the conducted mechanism in substations installed with SVC (Static Var Compensator) devices with a view to characterizing the main causes of the conducted interference. The high-frequency macro model for thyristors is established with a nonlinear time-varying resistor to simulate the switching characteristics of the thyristors. Based on the above macro model for thyristors, a concrete model of SVC including TSC (Thyristor-switched Capacitor) and TCR (Thyristor-controlled Reactor) is further proposed. In addition, high-frequency equivalent models for frequency-domain compensation of both CT and PT, based on their calibrated non-flat amplitude-frequency characteristics, are adopted to rectify the emissions levels from the SVC switching. The conducted interferences by simulations are correlated with that from on-site measurements, which indicates that the high-frequency switching characteristics of thyristors are the main causes of conducted emissions.

articleTitle: Design of Digital Filter Using Improved Prewarping Method
abstract: A new digital filter design method based prewarping is proposed , the digital filter frequency characteristic very well approximated to the original analog filter one' s, and two design examples of the BW (butterworth) filter and the elliptic filter are presented. The results of computer simulation are consistent with the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Measurement and analysis of Electromagnetic Fields Radiated by Corona Discharge
abstract: Corona discharge is a usual type of electrostatic discharge (ESD). Electromagnetic fields radiated by corona discharge could be harm to microelectronic devices of airplane and weapon systems. In this paper, corona discharge current is studied in theory and its characteristics are developed by the analysis of measurement data. Moreover, experiment simulation system of corona discharge is built for simulating corona discharge of spatial objects. Further, the characteristics of electromagnetic fields radiated by corona discharge are developed by time-frequency technology and wavelet analysis methods.

articleTitle: Mirror Reflections in EMF Dosimetry
abstract: The paper discusses influence of conducting media upon EMF measurement and calibration EMF probes in a TEM cell due to mirror reflections. The same phenomenon exists while an (biological) object is exposed to EMF in the cell; it affects the power absorption by the object.

articleTitle: The EMC Analysis and Estimation Method for Complicated Electromagnetic Radiation System
abstract: Put forward a method of behavioral simulation in order to analyzing radiation of complicated electromagnetic radiation system. Introduce a way of building a relation matrix to assaying the connection between radiation sources and radiation path. Make use of the method analyzing and resolving the problem that the radiation intensity of a complicated electromagnetic radiation system went beyond the limit of state. Simulation and practice results show that the behavioral method is right and reliable and it can be used in EMC problem of multi-device complex systems.

articleTitle: The Application on Active Noise Cancellation - Research on the Series-Parallel Compensated UPS Converter
abstract: Based on the double three-phase bridge AC-DC PWM converter topology, this paper takes the series-parallel compensated UPS as APF to compensate harmonic in power system. Corresponding control strategies are studied. The decoupling control strategy of dq axis dual-loop based on direct current control scheme is used. To the problem of input voltage imbalances and harmonic voltage in non-ideal power supply, a control method with an input harmonic voltage feed-forward in dq0 frame is taken. The experimental results prove that the series-parallel compensated UPS can effectively improve the power quality.

Author Keywords: Double three-phase bridge PWM AC-DC converters

articleTitle: Characterization of Electric Field Pulses Produced by Cloud and Ground Lightning Discharges
abstract: We examined microsecond-and submicrosecond-scale pulses in electric field records of cloud and cloud-to-ground lightning discharges acquired in summer 2006, in Gainesville, Florida. A total of 12 cloud and 12 ground flashes were analyzed in detail, with the electric field record length being 96 or 200 ms and sampling interval being 4 or 10 ns. The majority of pulses in both cloud and ground discharges analyzed in this study were associated with the initial breakdown process and were relatively small in amplitude and duration. The typical durations were an order of magnitude smaller than tens of microseconds characteristic of "classical" preliminary breakdown pulses. We estimated that 26% of the pulses in the 12 cloud discharges and 22% of the pulses in the 12 cloud-to-ground discharges had total durations less that 1 μs.

articleTitle: Analysis and Optimization of the Frequency Selectivity for the Short-wave Radio Station Receiver System
abstract: In this paper, the model of an existing superheterodyne receiver system with poor performance is built and solved in order to depict the frequency selectivity curve of the entire receiver system. In addition, the main intermodulation products which will bring strong power and fall into the actual receiving channels are theoretically predicted. Meanwhile, to effectively suppress the potential interference signal among each part, the method of optimizing the frequency selectivity of sub-components (such as filters) is presented. Finally it achieves to the whole system selectivity optimization and reinforces the electromagnetic compatibility. The simulation results fully demonstrated that this optimized system shows the great effect of electromagnetic compatibility reinforcement.

articleTitle: Accuracy in Wideband Direction of Arrival System
abstract: Direction finding is one of the important aspects of electronic intelligence (ELINT) systems. This paper concentrates on a sample of wideband direction-finding (DF) with accuracy of 5deg rms, using conventional amplitude comparison technique in the X and Ku bands. Determining azimuth angle of arrival as the main task of DF system is affected by some sources of error. This paper addresses different sources of error and determines the amount of error in degrees due to each source and provides solution to compensate for it.

articleTitle: Selection of the Standard Antenna for the Validation of Antenna Test Range
abstract: The standard antenna method is one of the main methods for the validation of antenna test range. It is easily implemented since it doesn't need any special equipment, and it costs less workload and time. So it is believed that the standard antenna method will have a good prospect of application. The suitable type of the standard antenna for the standard antenna method is studied in the paper. Several antennas are designed, simulated and compared. Besides, the influence of the measurement accuracy of antenna dimensions on the measurement results of the antenna performance is discussed. Finally, based on an overall consideration of various factors, the pyramidal horn is proposed as the suitable standard antenna type for the standard antenna method.

articleTitle: LCL Characteristics of Parallel Transmission Line with Load Circuit
abstract: In Japan, a power-line communication (PLC or PLT) system was approved only as an in-house system. One of concerned matters is leakage electromagnetic fields from power lines, which are mainly caused by common-mode currents. The common-mode current should be estimated under a condition of LCL (Longitudinal Conversion Loss) of 16 dB in the Japanese rule. In this paper, the characteristics of LCL are discussed at an input terminal of two-parallel line, which is modeled after a simple inhouse power line, with unbalanced load circuit on a viewpoint of transmission-line theory. By applying an equivalent expression concerning common and differential modes at outlet terminals, the analysis is developed.

articleTitle: Research on the Influence of Several Parameters on Lightning Radiation Field
abstract: After reviewing the calculation of lightning radiation electromagnetic field above perfect conductor ground, the expression of the lightning radiation field above lossy ground is derived rigorously in this paper. Based on above two cases, the effect of the height of lightning channel, observation point height, and soil resistivity on the lightning radiation magnetic field are analyzed respectively. With the increase of lightning channel height, the curve of the resulting radiation magnetic field tends more seriously to negative z direction. Further experiment is necessary to ascertain the effect of finite channel height. Both the effect of observation point height less than 200 m on lightning radiation magnetic field and that of soil resistivity less than 10kΩΩm can be neglected.

articleTitle: Mobile Radio Base Stations and Handsets Radiation Effects: Analysis, Simulations and Mitigation Techniques
abstract: Considering mobile radio communication, we are all witnesses to the tremendous increase of the number of users, equipments and of the social, economic and security dominant impacts. Therefore improvements in the quality of service, power efficiency and reduction of parasitical interference and radiation are a must as presented in this paper. It is especially true for the new 3G and 4G cellular generations where the system handset power levels and bandwidth are increased. The mitigation techniques described in this paper for systems base stations and mobile handsets can contribute to the required improvements. However considerable more efforts are still needed in order to improve mobile radio communication to an efficient, secure and convenient system useful for the welfare and positive advancement of our global society.

articleTitle: 2007 Status of the Development of High-Power Electromagnetic (HPEM) Standards in the IEC
abstract: The International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) is the principal authority for world standards in electrical and electronics engineering. The IEC technical subcommittee 77C "High power transient phenomena" of technical committee 77 "Electromagnetic compatibility" is preparing standards and technical reports dealing with the High-altitude Electromagnetic Pulse (HEMP) and all categories of High-Power Electromagnetic (HPEM) threats including Intentional Electromagnetic Interference (IEMI). At present the work in IEC SC 77C comprises 20 projects, of which 17 have been published. Three new projects are underway and are summarized at the end of this paper. While this subject has been discussed in the past by this author, this paper is intended to document the current status in 2007.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Interference on Secondary Systems of Substation Caused by Short-circuit Fault
abstract: This paper analyzed the influences of different factors on the electromagnetic interferences applied on the secondary systems due to the short-circuit faults in substation. The secondary cables with sheath grounded in two terminals can effectively suppress the potential difference between the core and sheath of secondary cable. The influence of different factors on the potential difference between the core and sheath of secondary cable and sheath current are systematically studied in power frequency short-circuit fault. Analysis results show, when the secondary cable sheath is grounded in two terminals, the maximum potential differences applied on the insulation layer of the secondary cable can reach about 40% of the ground potential rise.

articleTitle: Analysis of Passive Interference on Radio Station from UHVDC Power Transmission Lines in Short-wave Frequency
abstract: The paper analyses passive interference on radio station from the ±800kV UHV power transmission lines because of electromagnetic scattering on the UHV power transmission lines, overhead ground and iron tower caused by external electromagnetic field, with the moment method NEC programming based on wire antenna calculation theory. The conclusion has been obtained that passive interference on radio station is around 1dBμV/m in 1MHz-30MHz and tabling the passive interference protecting distance proposes.

articleTitle: Frequency Selective Surface absorber loaded with lumped-element
abstract: A new type active FSS absorber which contains a conducting back-plane has been investigated. The reactive layer of the FSS absorber is perfect conductor. Lumped-element devices are loaded on the periodic units. Resonant frequency of the absorber depending on the lumped-element' resistance could shift in a specified frequency band.The bandwidth of the absorber with reflection loss below -20 dB can cover from 6 GHz to 12 GHz.

articleTitle: Fast Calculation of Radiated Emissions from Arbitrarily Shaped PCB with IC/LSI
abstract: This paper describes fast calculation of radiated emissions from an arbitrarily shaped printed circuit board (PCB). The radiated emissions from the PCB edge are calculated by taking into account magnetic surface current based on the field equivalent principle. The electric field at the PCB edge is provided by a fast algorithm the authors have proposed for power-bus resonance in the PCB. The calculation of radiated emission was completed within a few minutes and in good agreement with finite difference time domain (FDTD) calculation. In addition, an EMI simulation was demonstrated by using a linear macro model of IC/LSI. The calculation results were found to be in good agreement with the measurements.

articleTitle: A Framework of Automatic Testing System for Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In virtual of the complexities of traditional EMC tests, this paper introduces a framework of automatic testing system for electromagnetic compatibility. Furthermore, some method and ideals on data analysis are presented. The method provides much reliable basis on diagnosing EMC problems. It is much more convincible that this test framework is able to meet most EMC test requirements.

articleTitle: Corona Characteristics under Lightning Surges
abstract: An analysis is made for the attenuation and distortion of lightning surges traveling on overhead transmission lines under the corona condition. The corona characteristics are described by the q-u curves. The parameters of the surge waveshapes are varied experimentally to examine their effects on the q-u curves. A discussion about the experimental data is presented with emphasis on the corona onset voltage gradient, dynamic capacitance of the line conductor and energy losses of corona. It provides the foundation for accurate calculation of lightning overvoltages.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Wave Transmission in the Three-Layer-Model of Body
abstract: The human body, a partial electromagnetic compatibility system, was facing the harassment challenge of environmental electromagnetic waves. For the more thorough understanding of electromagnetic wave biological effect, this article constructed three media models of the human body, and discussed the energy loss conditions in several media and the relations between the incident and refracted electromagnetic waves. And then each layer' s theoretical expressions of reflect and transmit' s coefficient was worked out by using analytical method. Finally, the concrete electromagnetic environment was discussed, and the result of specific absorption rate was given in this paper.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Interference Prediction in Transient Electromagnetic Environment
abstract: This paper presents an approach to predict the interference effects of a transient electromagnetic environment (EME) caused by an aggregate of wideband transmitters on a traditional narrowband victim. Due to the constraint of the narrowband receiver, it is sufficient to evaluate such wideband parameters of transmitter as effective isotropically radiated average power (EIRP) and antenna gains, etc. at the center frequency of the victim. Consequently, the single frequency propagation models used in traditional radio link calculations has been utilized in conjunction with the models described in this paper to estimate the basic transmission loss over the propagation path from the wideband transmitter to the narrowband receiver, and consequently to calculate the interference power at the victim.

articleTitle: Reserch on the Mechanism of WRAN Self-Coexistence
abstract: It is common sense that coexistence is a key issue for the performance of any wireless technology which intends to operate in unlicensed band. WRAN(Wireless Regional Area Network) is a novel air interface (i. e., MAC and PHY) standards based on Cognitive Radios(CRs) defined by IEEE 802.22 Work Group(WG). It aims to reuse the fallow-TV spectrum without causing any harmful interference to incumbents (i.e., the TV receivers). This paper focuses on the WRAN self-coexistence performance analysis. Through researching the synchronization mechanism in MAC layer, we validate the synchronization convergence rule via modeling and simulation. The simulation results show that a lot of cells can convergence quickly in a square area even they work distributed completely.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Interference on Secondary Systems of Substation Caused by Incoming Lightning Stroke
abstract: The uniform numerical method is proposed to analyze the transient performances of grounding system with grounded secondary cable. The influences of different factors on the electromagnetic interferences applied on the secondary systems due to the lightning current invading into the substation, including materials of grounding electrodes, lightning current wave-shape, and the parameters of secondary cables. The length of the secondary cable has strong influence on the transient potential difference between the core and the shielding sheath of secondary cable.

articleTitle: Analyzing and Calculating Isolation between Antennas on Airplane Wireless System
abstract: The coupling of antennas is the major manner of electromagnetic interference (EMI) among wireless systems. Isolation between antennas is a primary parameter for electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) on airborne platform. Airborne platform is a complicate and large dimension object, and it is difficult to measure the isolation between antennas in whole working wideband. Based on the analysis and discussion of practical model, the isolation between two antennas is calculated by FEM and MoM separately. And the numerical results are compared with measurements and employed to speculate statement in whole frequency band in this paper. Then change of isolation is analyzed following the different of distance between two antennas.

articleTitle: A New Method of Positioning Interference in GSM-R Networks
abstract: A new testing method, two-point positioning of interference (TPPI), is introduced and compared with the conventional mode. Aiming at different types of interference in GSM-R networks, this paper analyzes how to make use of TPPI. Finally, analyzes the uncertainty of TPPI.

articleTitle: The Modeling Method of Interference Source of System-level Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In order to improve and reinforce the facilities with problems on electromagnetic compatibility, it is inevitable to get down to the suppression and improvement to the interference source first. If the computer modeling to the interference source could be undertaken before the correctness, then by means of simulation the best method is to be found to improve facilities, as a result of which the project cycle and the cost will be shortened and decreased. The thesis aims at introducing one modeling method to interference source of electromagnetic compatibility and studies the interference intensity between different system levels. Based on the built model of interference source, different suppression methods proposed based on different system levels can be simulated and compared. The approach aims at exploring the best way to improve the facilities before the actual action.

articleTitle: Modeling with NURBS surfaces used for RCS computation of electrically large objects
abstract: The non-uniform rational B-spline (NURBS) model is constructed based on the data points on the surface of a target, and the B-Spline basis functions are analyzed. The radar cross section (RCS) is calculated with the physical optics (PO) and LUDWIG integral method based on NURBS models, which verifies the validity of the modeling method mentioned in this paper.

articleTitle: Harmonic Analysis of HVDC Transformer using Harmonic Balance - Finite Element Method (HB-FEM)
abstract: Harmonic balance analysis is a powerful numerical method for solving nonlinear electromagnetic (EM) problems. It is also can be used to solve the nonlinear quasi-static electromagnetic field for DC biased transformer problems used in HVDC Transmission system and power electronics. This paper introduces a relatively new numerical method, namely, the harmonic balance-finite element method (HB-FEM) and its application to time-periodic steady-state nonlinear EM field problems. The validation of DC biased problem in nonlinear magnetic field and harmonic analysis are also presented in this paper.

articleTitle: The Analysis of Crosstalk of Parallel Crewel
abstract: Crosstalk between parallel wires frequently appears in electrical system. It can affect performance of the system. So the crosstalk is necessary to be analyzed. In this paper, based on the mode of parallel crew, we analyze the crosstalk problem with the method that transforms field into circuit. Thus, formula about near electric field coupling of parallel crew is presented for the first time. To prove correctness of the formula, using this formula proves situation which has been studied by former scholar. Then, the crosstalk is simulated with software, Mat lab and Multisim, under two different situations (i.e. same grounding find different grounding of parallel), so as to analyze the influence of grounding to the crosstalk. The results obtained from experiment of the crosstalk are identical with the simulation. Finally, method of restraining crosstalk is presented for practical project.

articleTitle: Method of Systemic EMC Evaluation
abstract: Systemic electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) evaluation method is presented in the paper. Firstly, the relative of all sensitive sub-systems and mathematical models of systemic EMC performance EMC(s) are provided. Secondly, this paper proposes a series, parallel, three basic hybrid sensitive ports electromagnetic compatibility prediction model and its mathematical model. Based on these models, the compatibility probability of all sensitive sub-systems can be analyzed and computed so as that systemic EMC performance EMC(s) can be computed successfully. Finally, systemic EMC(s) evaluation of a kind of military computer is provided as a typical application.

articleTitle: Analysis of Radiation Reduction of Coupled Microstrip Lines By Additional Via Fences
abstract: The paper analyzes the technique based on two additional grounded via fences with which the radiation can be reduced and controlled. The finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method has been used to simulate the complex structure. The obtained results indicate that the radiation can be controlled by adjusting the diameter of the via and increasing the via diameter can decrease the radiation.

articleTitle: Crosstalk Analysis of High Speed Digital Microstrip Traces over a Slotted Ground Plane Using the Non-uniform FDTD Method
abstract: The non-uniform finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method is presented to analyze the crosstalk of high speed digital microstrip traces over a slotted ground plane in this paper. The crosstalk influence factors including rise time of the high speed digital signal, slot width and trace to trace distance are analyzed. Further, the effect of reducing crosstalk between 3W Rule and guard trace grounded at two ends or at multipoint along it is compared. The conclusions of this paper could be applied to high speed digital printed circuit board (PCB) design.

articleTitle: Graphical electromagnetic computing method combined with IGES files import
abstract: In this paper, the graphical electromagnetic computing (GRECO) method combined with an interface that can identify and read IGES files is presented. Graphical electromagnetic computing (GRECO) is an effective method of predicting the radar cross section (RCS) of complex targets, but there must beforehand be a model file from which the shape parameter can be easily obtained. Based on the GRECO method, the non uniform rational B-spline surfaces (NURBS) modeling files generated by several geometric computer aided design programs through the IGES standard (initial graphics exchange specification) could be converted to the type fitting for the RCS calculation. Combined wi th IGES files import, the GRECO method's application range is extended.

articleTitle: Prediction of Common-mode Radiation from Printed Circuit Boards with Interconnections
abstract: In order to estimate the amount of common-mode radiation from a printed circuit board with low calculation cost, a common-mode antenna model has been developed. This paper demonstrates the application of the model to a board interconnection via a connector that is known to be a possible source of common-mode radiation. The radiated emissions estimated by the model agreed with the measurements for practical use.

articleTitle: Analysis of crosstalk between snakelike circuits in proximity
abstract: The adaptation of a transmission-line model to the prediction of crosstalk in the snakelike circuits is presented. This form of the solution gives insight into the various factors that contribute to the crosstalk occurred in the irregular distributed circuits. Numerical computations are presented to illustrate the model' s effect.

articleTitle: Development of the Measuring System for Lightning Current on High Tower
abstract: A kind of measuring system designed for the measurement of lightning return stroke currents under 50 kA, which is composed of current transformers, optical isolation system, data acquisition card and industrial computer, is described. Test results show that the current transformers and the optical isolation system have good stability. Moreover, primary research on remote transmission of the data is done. A wavelet-based compression arithmetic is designed, which is suitable for the data compression, greatly improving the speed of the data transmission.

articleTitle: Effects of Harsh Electromagnetic Environment on Inertial Measurement Unit of a Flight Vehicle
abstract: Verifying output pulse errors and upsets of an inertial measurement unit (IMU) in harsh electromagnetic environment (EME) is a key issue for inertial navigation and guidance system accurately measuring attitude angular rates and apparent accelerations of flight vehicle. This paper deals with an amount of laboratory tests on the IMU in a harsh EME, and performs a statistical analysis with the measured data to characterize the degree of EME effects on the IMU upsets and assess how the effects of the EME on the variations of the output pulses number from IMU sensors or inertial instruments such as gyroscopes and accelerometers.

articleTitle: Research on Performance of Frequency-hopping Radio Services by Using Statistical Method
abstract: This paper presents a novel method to evaluate performance of frequency-hopping radio receivers affected by a disturbance by using statistical results of the disturbance. The statistical results of interfering signals, especially amplitude probability distribution (APD), have been widely used, and the relationship between the statistical results and performance of digital radio systems has been an open issue. In this paper we show that the amplitude statistics of disturbance have significant influence on the bit error probability (BEP) of the victim while frequency hopping is off, and then we give out the evaluating model while frequency hopping is on. The model is evaluated by simulations with a Bluetooth victim.

articleTitle: Measurement of Pulsed Electric Field Shielding Effectiveness of Reinforced Grids Cubic Cages
abstract: It presents a measurement of pulsed electric field by way of portable measurement system for the shielding effectiveness of pulsed electric field, tn order to research the influence of bonding method of cross points of reinforced grids and the size of reinforced grids, three bonding methods and two types of reinforced grids' size are evaluated in this measurement. Then the results of experiment are obtained. In addition, some valuable conclusions are reached, which can be applied to engineering.

articleTitle: shielding Effectiveness of Metal Door in Circular Tunnel to Non-unclear EMP
abstract: In this paper, a body of revolution finite difference time domain (BOR-PDTD) is introduced. The shielding effectiveness of metal door in circular tunnel to non-nuclear electromagnetic pulse (HPM and UWB) in protective engineering is analyzed. The numerical results showed good agreement with those obtained from experiment, and some valuable conclusions are obtained.

articleTitle: Novel view: frequency spectrum and harmonic distortion of FM signal based on DDS
abstract: Direct digital frequency modulated (DDFM) signal, which certainly on the direct digital synthesizers is widely used in EMC test and measurement. This paper analytically expressed the frequency spectrum of DDFM signal. Works of this paper also include: modifies the approximate formula for first order harmonic distortion (FHD) and discovers restrictions.

articleTitle: Impact of Cellular Phone Usage Duration on Power Control and Violation of EMC Regulations
abstract: This communication presents a study showing that cellular phone usage duration have got a significant effect on the power control in mobile cellular networks. This is because the long-time operation (transmitting and receiving) of the cellular phone radio hardware cause the wearing-out of radio elements. Hence, the operation of worn-out radio elements introduces power control errors and this degrades the performance of the power control algorithms. And this result in poor power control of the excessive transmitted power, hence the interference caused, compels a handset to violate the EMC regulations. This degrades the quality of the mobile cellular services. The paper also presents a derived power control performance model for a handset.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of Smart Mobile Terminal Antennas for Wireless Communication and Computing Systems
abstract: The paper presents an electronically beam switched smart mobile terminal antenna (SMTA) array used in wireless network. SMTA arrays were optimized for the secured communication performance and desired radiation coverage. The radiation beam pattern toward desired direction is controlled by switched beam control algorithm. Four different configurations of SMTA arrays and their design considerations are discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Methods on Further Improving the Spectrum Management
abstract: The article abstractly describes some points of methods on further improving of the spectrum efficiency. At first, the author introduces the current challenges facing spectrum management, spectrum circumstance and the traditional regulatory framework of doing this in China. Then the importance of raising the spectrum efficiency and some technical methods are analyzed in the article. The strategy of the spectrum management and the spectrum-sharing technology are also briefly discussed. The need of the different field on the frequency spectrum policy reforming and the trends of development are discussed in the end.

articleTitle: Critical distance of far field for basic radiation element
abstract: The paper provides a new method to determine the critical distance of the far-field (FF) of a basic radiation element by calculating the relative error between approximate and exact FF values in three respects: field value in maximum radiation direction; the pattern of FF and wave impedance .The result is obtained and recommended as critical distance of the basic radiation element, which is approached engineering requirement and calculation process is reduced largely. It can be widely used in antenna analysis and EMC prediction.

articleTitle: Study on the Granularity Effect on Electromagnetic Wave Absorbing Properties of Ni-SiC Composites
abstract: In order to solve electromagnetic compatibility and interference problems in electromagnetic defence field, the Ni-SiC. composites were prepared. The effects of Ni-SiC particles with different granularities on absorbing properties at the frequency range from 8 GHz to 18.4 GHz and their absorption mechanism were studied. The research results show that the changes of granularities of Ni-SiC particles have obvious influences on absorbing properties. When the granularities of the same kind of particles reduce to a certain scale, the test results show different absorbing properties. In the Ni-SiC composites, the absorbing properties of 5.48μm SiC are better than those of 10.39μm SiC and 21μm SiC under the same composition. It is found that the minimum reflectivity of 5.48μm SiC is -16dB and the bandwidth for -10dB is 3GHz. The absorption mechanism of the Ni-SiC composites is magnetic and dielectric loss and scattering effect.

articleTitle: Research of the Characteristics of Radio Wave Propagations around the High-Speed Railway
abstract: High-speed railway is the trend of our national railway. Research of the radio wave propagation is very important for the development of railway wireless communication system. In the paper, the simulation model of channel is formed using the theory of sine superposition. The parameters of the model are confirmed using the method of equidistance. Then, on the base of this channel, the characteristics of radio wave propagations of high-speed railway are analysed. At last, the relevant conclusions are given.

articleTitle: Weighted Laguerre Polynomials and its Applications in Transient RCS Analysis
abstract: Weighted Laguerre polynomial is a set of self-contained orthogonal causal functions. In this paper, the properties of weighted Laguerre polynomials are summarized. As a set of temporal basis functions, the influence and choice of the time scaling factor are discussed in detail. And then the choice principle for the time scaling factor is obtained. The application of weighted Laguerre polynomials, which are the temporal basis of transient scattering analysis for arbitrary shaped structures, is illustrated for transient RCS calculation. The examples show that the choice principle proposed here is effective.

articleTitle: Circuit Model for Two Parallel Microstrip Lines on Slotted Ground Plane
abstract: A transmission-characteristic analysis of two parallel microstrip lines on PCB with a slotted ground plane is studied. When two trace lines are very closed, crosstalk occurs between them. In addition to it, magnetic-field coupling between the traces and the slot line also exists. In this paper, a circuit model for transmission characteristics of such line system is proposed. The calculated results are compared with the experimental results to veryfy the proposed model.

articleTitle: Research and Application of the System on Measuring Magnetic Field in Complicated EMI Environment in Substation
abstract: In order to test the corrosion degree and broken points of grounding grids, being aimed at the distribution characteristics of the surface magnetic fields, a special system of measuring the surface megnetic imduction imtensities is designed based on analyzing the practical EMI environment in substation. Using by this system, the surface magnetic field distrbutions is measured by Faraday electromagnetic induction theorem. Experimental and practical researchs show that this diagnosis method is feasible, the system is pratical and reliable. The dignosis efficiency and precision are improved.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Emanations of the ICs
abstract: This paper presents an investigation of the leakage of compromising information via electromagnetic (EM) emanations from cryptographic modules or other ICs. The paper describes the work characters of static CMOS gates firstly. Based on the concrete circuit which was realized with an AT89C52 microchip, we made experiments of near field measurements to the EM emanation of the AT89C52 module. The result of the experiments shows that there is data-EM emanation correlation for working ICs.

articleTitle: Optimization of Calibration Procedure for Reverberation Chamber Based on NI LabVIEW Platform
abstract: As an alternative technique, reverberation chamber has been more and more accepted and applied for EMC test, especially for EMS tests for electronic equipment, ordnance electronics and also advanced MIMO technologies for wireless communication. In this paper, the test standards are first analyzed and compared. Secondly, by considering the economy and time saving factors, an optimized programming procedure and program structure are designed and presented for realizing the calibration test based on NI LabVIEW platform. Finally, some experimental results for a newly built reverberation chamber are presented.

articleTitle: Comparison Between High Altitude EMP and High Power Electromagnetic Effects on Equipment and Systems
abstract: The electromagnetic effects of a High Altitude EMP has been a threat for communications and installations which has been largely studied and documented between 1960 and 1990. During the last decade of the 20th century, a new kind of electromagnetic field representing a new threat, has been developed, the High Power Electromagnetic (HPEM) field. The paper will discuss and compare the main features of these two kind of electromagnetic fields, like the spatial coverage, the frequency spectrum, the time-domain behavior and will briefly compare the protection measures which can be taken against these two kind of electromagnetic effects.

articleTitle: Comparison of Radiated Susceptibility of a Digital IC between Electric Field Coupling and Magnetic Field Coupling Based on a Circuit Apparoach
abstract: In this study, the radiated susceptibility of a microstrip line with a digital IC is investigated. A circuit approach is used by converting external incident electric and magnetic fields into equivalent current and voltage sources, respectively, and the interference voltages induced at IC pins are simulated by using a circuit simulator. As a result, it is found that the digital IC exhibits a higher susceptibility for the magnetic field coupling compared to the electric field coupling.

articleTitle: Implementing APD Measurement in Monolithic Circuits
abstract: As a new measuring method for the frequency range 1 GHz to 18 GHz, amplitude distribution probability (APD) method had been formally written into CISPR 16-1-1 Ed. 2: Specification for radio disturbance and immunity measuring apparatus and methods in 2005. For the traditional EMI receivers that are employed widely in most EMC test labs, additional measuring apparatus were necessary to implementing APD measurement. Herein, we introduced an APD measuring apparatus that developed by EMC Research Section, Beijing Jiaotong University, PRC. This apparatus was designed based on fast analog-digital conversion and VLSI technology. All the digital logic function was built in a single field programmable gate arrays (FPGA) device. And all of the specification meets the requirements of CICPR16-1-1.

articleTitle: Study on the Propagation Characteristics of the Radio Noise form Electric Railway in Shortwave Band
abstract: In this paper, the simulation and measurement is done in order to research the transverse attenuation characteristics of the radio disturbance form the electrified railway in the shortwave band. Comparison is made between the simulation results and measurement results. It is concluded that the radio noises produced by the electric railway in the shortwave band should not influence the field transmitted by the antenna 120 m away.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Numerically Computed Spatial Peak SAR Values in Uniformly Scaled SAM Head Models Exposed to Mobile Phone Radiation
abstract: Numerical simulations were conducted to investigate dependence of spatial peak SAR values on head size, and thus reach a conclusion whether child heads absorb more radiation than that of adult ones. A dipole and a generic phone model were used to simulate real mobile phone at 900/835 MHz. The standard SAM phantom represents adult head model. Three child head models were derived after uniformly scaling SAM head in all directions by 90%, 80% and 70%. The experiment results showed that smaller head models produce statistically higher spatial peak SAR values than larger ones. The conclusion is contrary to the results of recent international research study which suggested larger head models tend to show statistically higher spatial peak SAR values than smaller ones. The maximum increase in peak SAR of up to 16% was observed in smallest head compared to that in SAM original head. We noticed relative positions have significant influence on such trend. Post-processing normalization is another important factor to be considered while making comparison. SAR results normalized to antenna current showed small dependence on head size compared to those normalized to antenna power.

articleTitle: State of Art of the EMC Standardization for Power Line Communication
abstract: During the last two years, very little progress has been achieved in the field of standardization pertaining to PLC. But since 2006 a New Work Item Proposal has been accepted for CISPR I by the National Committees and two documents have been published. The Joint Working Group ETSI/CENELEC on the network standard has frozen the work due to disagreement on field limits radiated generally by communication networks. However, new initiatives with a New Work Item Proposal have been taken in CENELEC, namely in Working Group 10 of the SC205A. The development of coexistence standards is making good progress. The regulatory procedures in the EU for in-house and access PLC are briefly introduced.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Transient Grounding Resistance Characteristics on a Spokewise Grounding Electrode
abstract: The characteristics of transient voltage, current and grounding resistance of a spokewise grounding electrode is investigated based on field measurements. The grounding electrode is composed of 8 reinforcing steel bars with diameter of 10 mm, every bar with the length of 2 m, and is buried at the depth of 0. 6 m from the ground surface. A pulse discharge from a high-voltage capacitor is applied at the center of the grounding electrode to observe transient voltage and current on it. The measured results are illustrated, the transient grounding resistance is calculated and analyzed.

articleTitle: Discussion on Electromagnetic Compatibility Index for Secondary System of Substation
abstract: This paper discussed the characteristic parameters of the electromagnetic environment (EME) of substation. According to the general demands to EME for secondary devices in substation, the demands to the EMC immunity test for secondary devices in substation are proposed, which satisfy the EMC characteristics of substation.

articleTitle: Recognition Method of Radar Signal Based on Rough Set and Support Vector Machine
abstract: A hybrid algorithm based on attributes reduction of rough set and classification principles of support vector machine (SVM) is presented in this paper. Firstly, the attributes reduction of rough set has been applied as preprocessor so that we can delete the redundant attributes and conflicting objects from decision making table but remain efficient information lossless. Then, the classification modeling and forecasting test based on SVM are realized. By this method, the dimension of data is reduced greatly, the complexity in the process of SVM classification is decreased highly, the occupied memory is cut down and the over-fit of training model is prevented at some extent, also the good classification performance is obtained. Finally, the simulation experiment of radar signal recognition and its results show this hybrid method is effective.

articleTitle: Site-Specific Propagation Prediction for UWB Indoor Non-line-of-sight environment
abstract: A site-specific propagation prediction for UWB impulse signals within indoor non-line-of-sight (NLOS) environment is addressed in this paper. The transmitter and the receiver are placed in two rooms respectively with a concrete wall blocking the line-of-sight (LOS) propagation path. The simulation utilizes the principles of geometrical optics (GO) for reflected and transmitting paths' tracing and time domain technique for describing the transient electromagnetic field transmitting through as well as reflected from the wall, the floor, the ceiling, and the objects. Based on the simulation results, the time dispersion as well as antenna effect for the received impulse signals within the NLOS environment is analysed.

articleTitle: Research on the model for EMC problem of receiver at the same frequency band
abstract: In this paper, the mathematic model of receiver about electromagnetic compatibility is described. The basic process about effectiveness evaluation is given, and receiver models on every evaluation process are built.

articleTitle: GPS Anti-Jamming Modeling and Simulation Analysis for Navigation System Based on Antenna Array
abstract: In this paper, the navigation model combining GPS and INS is detailedly analyzed, whose extended Kalman filter (EKF) algorithm is given. The principle and mathematical model of multiple MVDR beamforming is given. On the basis of this, the anti-jamming model of navigation system based on GPS/INS and antenna array is proposed. The simulation results show that the position error of single beamforming technique because of the limited degree of freedom with the large of interference signals is greater than multiple beamforming technique, and that multiple MVDR beamforming can effectively mitigate a number of interference signals and ensure the reliability working of navigation system.

articleTitle: Modeling and Characteristic of the Vertical Bonding-Wire Interconnection for Millimeter Wave
abstract: This paper announced a new type of bonding interconnect---vertical bonding interconnect. Bonding interconnect is the critical technique for realizing the interconnect of microwave chip. The height, distance, number of wires and joint space of bonding interconnect have important effects on its microwave characteristics. In this paper, commercial 3D electromagnetic analysis software HFSS, microwave circuit design software ADS and Agilent vector network analyzer were used to model, simulate and optimize for the microwave characteristics of bonding interconnect, and produce the model, experimental results shown in this paper.

articleTitle: Aerial and buried cables lightning protection with assistance of earth connection
abstract: In this paper are discussed some ways of lightning protection communication cables, such as protective conductor laying close to communication cable and making an earth connection to metal envelope of cable in some points along line. It is touching as aerial or buried optical or electrical with copper cores small-capacity cable. A part of this data was published in Russian, but is unknown to English-speaking specialists.

articleTitle: EMI Analysis for Two Types of Radar on the Same Platform
abstract: On limited space of the same platform, more and more radio electronic equipment are increased, which results in more problems of electromagnetic compatibility(EMC) that almost all of them caused by antenna mutual-coupling. As the example of two radar on the same platform, this paper gives the EMC test data in each carrier frequency band. Through the test data analysis it can be concluded that the electromagnetic interference (EMI) caused by adjacent frequency channel interference, According to the results of spectrum measurement, when increasing the carrier frequency interval it can ensure the two radar works well compatibility.

articleTitle: Energy Absorption Mechanism of Head in the Near Field of Dipole
abstract: IEC, ETSI and other international standard organizations have drawn general standards for specific absorption rate (SAR) of EM radiation from various handle wireless communication equipment in the near field, and keeps on consummating related product standards. Comparing with the expensive and long time testing, the simulation technique has outstanding advantages, and it is applicable in terminal design, R&D and pre-authentication. In this paper, we take the dipole as a simple model to simulate the energy absorption mechanism of head in the near field by FDTD method, then compare and analyze with the experimental results, at last give some suggestion to improve the precision of simulation.

articleTitle: Model of Es Occurrence Probability in China at 1985 2006
abstract: The time percentage of Es occurrence has been studied in this paper, using the 22-year ionosphere sounding datasets from 1985 to 2006, involving 18 sites in China and the adjacent. The statistical characteristic for equinox (March, April, September, October), summer (May, June, July, August), winter (November, December, January, February) and annual average are listed. The correlations among Es occurrence probability (logarithm) and frequency and latitude and longitude are studied, and the frequency-dependence model and the geography-dependence model are established. Then the comparison between our model and data in ITU-R P.534-4 is given. Based on our models, region variation of Es occurrence probability is drawn for different seasons in China region

articleTitle: Using Smart Mobile Terminal Antennas to Achieve Optimal Wireless Network Performance and Security
abstract: In this paper, a complete smart mobile terminal antenna system (SMTA) is presented. This system uses a radiation beam switching approach in an attempt to achieve optimal wireless network performance while increasing network security. Test results are presented that demonstrate the ability of the SMTA system to maintain consistently high wireless signal levels in a dynamic, noisy environment.

articleTitle: A New Method of Measuring the Frequency Response Characteristics of A Loop
abstract: This paper introduces a new method of measuring the frequency response characteristics of a loop, which is measuring the mutual inductance and self- inductance of the loop to be measured and the single-turn loop which is close winded outside the former one to indirectly gain the frequency response characteristics of the loop to be measured. The method is simple, convenience and has low request to measuring environment. This paper introduces an example of measuring an actual loop in the end and the measuring result is in good agreement with the theoretical analysis result.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of the Coaxial-fed Cavity-backed Annular Slot Antenna
abstract: This article presents the design and analysis of a coaxial-fed cavity-backed slot antenna. The use of a parasitic annular slot for the annular-slot-excited dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) with a backing cavity is theoretically studied. Based on the finite element methods (FEM), the VSWR, input impedance, radiation characteristics and the parameters of the antenna were analyzed. The numerical calculations emphasize narrow slots and shallow cavities. Resonance frequency, bandwidths, and radiation patterns were studied with respect to a slot width, a cavity depth and the coaxial-fed position. By optimizing the parameters of the antenna, circular polarization and the bandwidth arranged from 250 MHz to 400 MHz with VSWR\5.0 were obtained.

articleTitle: Research on Distribution of Electric Field near Ground during Thunderstorm Process
abstract: In this paper, electric field near ground during thunderstorm process is discussed with field data measured by thunderstorm electric field mill and numerical simulation. The measured field data shows that the atmospheric field became strong as measure height increased. The cause is given out by the numerical simulation. And the result of numerical simulation shows accordance with measured data. The distribution details of electric field near ground are given out by the numerical simulation.

articleTitle: The Three-Dimensional Fast Algorithm of Solving the Electric Field Integral Equation
abstract: A fast algorithm is introduced in this paper for three-dimensional conducing medium. The algorithm applies suitable approximation and parallel computation to MoM so that the computer memory and run time will be reduced significantly. Finally, we calculate a three-dimensional thin lossy plate as an example to approve the accuracy and efficiency of our algorithm.

articleTitle: An Experimental Study on the Indoors Attenuation of Electromagnetic Wave for Transmitting the Standard Time Signal
abstract: This study experimentally clarifies that the causes by which the radio control clock sometimes fails to receive the standard time signal in the indoors are in the following two factors: (1) the shielding by the conductive materials (used for column, pillar, floor and so on) existing close to the radio control clock. (2) The missing of tuning and the change of Q of the antenna due to the closely existing conductive materials.

articleTitle: Calculation and Research of Electromagnetic Fields in Space Around Lightning Path with finite difference time domain method
abstract: In this paper, numerical calculation method based on analytical formulas and FDTD are studied. A physical model for nature lightning is built in this paper, the lightning channel as a long ling wire, lightning current' s double exponential pulse time domain waveform. The numerical method from dipole formula is obtained by scattering lightning current at time and space, With finite difference time domain(FDTD) method, lightning space is dispersed and electromagnetic fields for whole free space are solved, with the computer program, the results are consistent with results of references and simulating test.

articleTitle: Research on low reflection Material of double layer medium structure
abstract: Low reflection material is very useful in many applications. At present, the operation frequency in the most absorbing materials are above 4GHz, for it is difficult to realize the low reflection below 4GHz with thin structure<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>. A thin structure material that realize the low reflection was studied by using the analog circuit method in this issue. A genetic algorithm is used to find the optimization parameter. The simulations by equivalent circuit and FEM methods show a low reflection between 2 GHz and 9GHz, which is only 9mm thick and the value of reflection loss is lower than -6dB.

articleTitle: Application of Modified Transmission Line Equation to the Conductors within the Cavity Resonator
abstract: In this paper, the electromagnetic fields coupled with the conductors within the cavity resonator are investigated by using the modified transmission line equation. The modified equation is derived from the transmission line theory taking the effects of cavity resonator into account. The modified equation is solved and can be well applied to calculate the electromagnetic fields of such problem.

articleTitle: ABCD Network Function for Analysis of Crosstalk Between Microstrip Lines in Arbitrary Directions on Different Layers
abstract: A method for the analysis of crosstalk between two microstrip lines in arbitrary directions lying on different layers is proposed using a circuit-concept approach. Electromagnetic fields in a PCB substrate due to microstrip lines are estimated by using an image method and then those are applied to transmission line theory. To verify the proposed approach, we compared the results of our approach with those of a commercial electromagnetic solver.

articleTitle: Study on the Transmission of Multi-Ridge Waveguides based on Finite Element Method
abstract: Finite element method is introduced to analyze the transmission of multi-ridge waveguide, solves the cutoff wavelength of the dominant mode and field pattern of the typical model size in double ridge waveguides, triple ridge waveguides and quintupling ridge waveguides, analyzes the changes of the transmission by changed the multiple of ridges, the ridge width, the ridge height and the distance between ridges. Some computational data and figures are presented.

articleTitle: Effects of electromagnetic pulse on the vimentin of mice testes
abstract: To investigate the changes of the mice testes and the tight junction (Tj) relative molecular and to identify the molecular mechanisms of the mice blood-testis-barrier (BTB) permeability increasing after the mice were exposed to electromagnetic pulse (EMP). Observe the changes vimentin of the mice testes by laser scanning confocal technique. After the 200 kVm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> EMP (the accumulative pulse times was 200) exposure, the vimentin in sustentacular cells of testis became irregularly shortened and derangement, and the intensity of immuno-fluorescence also showed ununiformity compared with control. The increasing of mice BTB permeability perhaps caused by the changing of vimentin.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Channel Estimation Method Based on Doppler Shift Estimation in mobile WIMAX
abstract: An adaptive channel estimation method in 802. 16 e system, based on Doppler shift estimation, is proposed. The coherence time can be gotten through Doppler shift estimation. Then the time domain channel impulse response (CIR) gotten by least squares (LS) algorithm can be refined according to the correlation duration the coherence time. The simulation results in the frequency band of 2.4 GHz show that the proposed method achieves a good bit error rate (BER) performance according to the speed variance of the vehicles.

articleTitle: Calculation of Lightning Radiation Field Considering the Effect of Ionosphere
abstract: In this paper, the effect of ionosphere to the lightning radiation magnetic field is investigated using Sommerfeld integral. Supposing that the ionosphere is perfect conductor layer, the rigorous and simplified expressions of magnetic field are both obtained. Based on the engineering model, the obtained expression is applied to analyzing the characteristics of lightning radiation magnetic field. The analysis indicates that the reflection from the ionosphere results in multiple peaks in lightning radiation magnetic field. Accordingly, some of the subsequent peaks in the measurement of lightning radiation fields, usually taken as subsequent strokes, may result from the reflection of the ionosphere.

articleTitle: Effect of EMP on lipid peroxidation of human gastric cancer cells MKN28
abstract: AIM To discuss the effect of EMP on lipid peroxidation of human gastric cancer cells MKN28. METHODS MKN28 cells were divided into 5 groups (control group, 50, 100, 200, 400kV•-1groups), 16 wells for each group. 12 hours after the cell-planting, each group were exposed by 0, 50, 100, 200, 400kV•m-1 respectively. 0, 6, 12, 24, 48h after EMP irradiation, the wells of each group were separated and detected by chemiluminescence analysator. The result was recorded in forms of value of first peak and 5s integral area. The data obtained from the experiment were analyzed by ANOVA. RESULTS Compared with control group, the chemoluminescence intensity (value of first peak and 5s integral area) of 50, 100kV•-1 irradiation groups (0, 6, 24h after irradiation) and 200, 400kV•1 irradiation groups (0, 6, 12, 24, 48h after irradiation) decreased significantly (p<0.01). CONCLUSION Certain EMP irradiation can significantly decrease the level of lipid peroxidation of human gastric cancer cells MKN28.

articleTitle: Research of Dual-helical coupled slow-wave circuit Cold-Test Characteristics in CFA
abstract: In this paper the dispersive character of Crossed-Field Amplifier (CFA), with dual-helical coupled slow-wave structure, was simulated by using the "Microwave Studio" software from CST Company. Moreover, transfers character of stub-supported meander line slow-wave structure and dual-helical coupled slow-wave structure also is calculated and analyzed in C band. The result shows that this kind of slow-wave structure could completely meet the design requirements of CFA in C or X band. This paper's research established a foundation for the design of CFA working in C or X band.

articleTitle: An Improved Vector Fitting Method for Parametric Identification of Transfer Functions in EMC Measurement
Effects of EMP exposure on the memory function of rat pups
abstract: To determine whether exposure to electromagnetic pulses (EMP) emissions results in behavioral effects and evaluate memory function of rats pups. The Wistar rats, either male or female, were divided randomly into two groups respectively: control (CTR) and 104 pulses (G1). Then G1 group was exposed to EMP of 146. 5 kv/m field amplitude and 104 pulses. For the day of exposure till 3 months later, they were mated with the rats in the same group and their offspring were divided into two groups (F-GRT, F-G1) correspondingly. Our study was performed to determine if behavioral teratological changes occur in 3-month old rat pups. Offspring were examined in step through test, Y-maze and open-field test . Behavioral effects of EMP-expose were unremarkable with these exceptions: (1) In step through test, female pups in F-G1 group emitted a slightly increase in memory retention; (2) In y-maze test, all the pups in F-G1 significantly learned less times than control; (3) In open-field test, as compared with the control, both female and male pups in F-G1 group have significantly changes. Offspring of the rats exposed to 1 x 104 pulses performed better in learning and memory retention.

articleTitle: Relations of the Thunder-Stroke Selectivity and Earth Resistivity
abstract: The characteristics of thunder-rain cloud have been introduced after learning the lightning. Two factors of cloud-terra discharge have been analyzed. According to the model which is model of the cloud-terra capacitor simulating as parallel plate capacitor, based on the thunder electric current double index model and the Heidler model that was recommended by the International Electrician Commission in IEC1312-1 in 1995, the quantitative relations of the earth resistivity and first cloud-terra discharge lightning current amplitude value was reduced. There is a conclusion which the earth resistivity and first cloud-terra discharge lightning current amplitude value magnitude become the decreasing function relations. And the thunder-stroke selectivity has been investigated. It has provided the important reference to construct each kind of building and defense the lightning.

articleTitle: Suppressing EMI of Switching Converters Using Self-Excitation-Chaos
abstract: A method of EMI reduction using spectral modification through self-excitation-chaos is proposed. We derived a second-order S-switching iterative map describing the dynamics of simple feedback Buck switching regulator operating in continuous mode. Analysis of this map shows that chaos and bifurcations may occur at certain values of the input voltage. By making the converter operating in chaos, the simulation results demonstrate that a reduction of spectral peak and consequent spreading of the spectrum can be shown, and it will hardly influence to output voltage ripples.

articleTitle: Mie Series Study on Electromagnetic Scattering of Metallic Sphere Covered by Double-negative Metamaterials
abstract: How to overcome the instability of the two-layer dispersive media mie series formula is firstly discussed when the electric size of sphere is large. Then, the radar cross section of an impedanced-matched, ideal, homogeneous double-negative (DNG) metamaterials sphere is computed. The backward radar cross section of the DNG media sphere adds up to zero. The radar cross section of metallic sphere covered by DNG media or ferrite are compared. Numerical results show that DNG media can make the radar cross section of metallic sphere decrease just like ferrite.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Indoor Radio Channel Model
abstract: A multipath model of UWB pulse propagation in the indoor environment is addressed in this paper. The simulation utilizes the principles of geometrical optics (GO) for direct and reflected paths' tracing and time domain technique for describing the transient electromagnetic field reflected from wall, floor, ceiling, and objects. The closed-form time domain analytic solution for UWB impulse signal reflection, which takes into account the frequency range from 3. 1 to 10.6 GHz, is proposed, and it is suitable for dry concrete, wood, glass, etc. , which are envisioned as common building construction materials for indoor environment. A specific house with two cube-like objects, which is thought to be a more realistic environment, is investigated. The simulation results provide the three-dimension (3D) space-time distribution of received pulsed field, which give more intrinsically interpretations for the mechanics of UWB impulse signals propagation in indoor environment.

articleTitle: Analysis of the E-field Distribution for E-field Probes Calibration in Tissue-Simulating Liquid
abstract: In this paper, the E-field distribution in a waveguide partly filled with tissue-simulating liquid at mobile communications frequencies is presented. For the E-field probes calibration in the tissue-simulating liquid, a standing open rectangular waveguide partly filled with tissue-simulating liquid is used in which the E-field can be calculated analytically from input power measurements. It is desirable that the field distribution inside the tissue-simulating liquid follows the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> pattern.
