This has been verified by using the FDTD numerical technique and taking scan measurements at different heights from the dielectric spacer. The theoretical and simulating results are testified to be in good agreement with measurements.

articleTitle: Study on Suppression Technologies of the Electromagnetic Radiation of High Frequency welder
abstract: In this article, based on the Nation's Electromagnetic Compatibility Standard (GB4824-2004-2A), dealing with traditional High Frequency welder's severely exceeding the standard in its radiant intensity of its basic frequency, duplicate frequency and triplicate frequency, three measures come out: 1. to make a resonance circuit damper on the head of the Hot-sealing Machine, through the building of wave trap and choking field, to weaken and absorb the high radiant electromagnetic field, thus to weaken the intensity of the radiant field made by electromagnetic leak ; 2. to screen the high-frequency sheet copper feeder, using the technique of weakening and screening the electromagnetic radiation; 3. to redesign high-frequency oscillation circuit, thus to decrease harmonic made by surge. The result shows that after the inhibition of electromagnetic radiation, the output frequency of high frequency welder accords with nation's prescriptive frequency standard. It solves the problem of radiation pollution made by electromagnetic leek when high frequency Hot-sealing Machine is working.

articleTitle: A New Kind of Microstrip-Antenna with Two Parallel Coupling Apertures
abstract: A new kind of microstrip-antenna with two parallel coupling apertures is presented. It is based on ordinary aperture coupled microstrip-antenna, with one more set of aperture and feed line. After that a few performances of the antenna have improved to a certain extent. Simulation results and physical analysis are also given to support the effectiveness of this novel antenna.

articleTitle: Fast Sample Technique in Antenna Time Domain Near Field Measurement
abstract: In the practice of antenna time domain planar near field measurement, the probe moving step by step in each sample point is not acceptable for the huge time spending. The effect of measuring results in case of probe continuously moving in one dimension has been analyses in this paper. From simulation, it can be find that sample in the condition of probe moving continuously has almost the same measuring precision as sample in the condition of probe moving in step, and the probe moving speed can be even much faster than it in frequency domain. It means that time domain near field measurement can support fast sample, and has more efficiency than frequency domain near field measurement.

articleTitle: Study on Gas Discharge at Atmospheric Air by Numerical Method
abstract: The progress and characteristics of gas discharge is studied in this paper by numerical simulation. A program based on the FE-FCT method in its full two-dimension form is developed and employed for the solution of transport equations of charged species under the effect of space-charge electric field. Results of two-dimensional simulation of cylindrically symmetric streamers in air between Point-plane electrodes are presented. The formation and propagation of streamer is numerically observed. The electric field distribution, streamer speed, radius of streamer channel predicted by the model is in good agreement with experimental measurement. The influence of applied voltage on the streamer characteristic is also investigated.

articleTitle: The anti-jamming analysis and simulation to UWB - Multiband OFDM System Based on Simulink
abstract: This paper presents an overview analysis of EMC problems on a UWB system. After outlining the enormous potentialities of UWB systems and the benefits in terms of capacity and flexibility coming from their large bandwidth, then we analyze the dedicated UWB channel model. The simulation result is given in the end of the paper using the dedicated UWB channel.

articleTitle: A Wide Band Coherent Ice Penetrating Radar Receiver and Related EMC Considerations
abstract: We have accomplished a prototype of wide band Coherent ice penetrating radar system which can be used for polar ice depth measurement. The radar uses pulse compression and Coherent integration techniques and works in the VHF band. Using different transmit power, the system can operate in both surface-based and airborne applications. A dual-channel receiver is introduced for better performance on different layer' s return signals. Related EMC considerations are also given.

articleTitle: The Application of Choke in Parabola Antennas
abstract: Decreasing width and increasing gain on the main lobe of parabola antenna are important tasks in design. This paper discusses choke restraining on back radiation of parabola antennas. It improves radiation performance of the parabola antenna excited by circular waveguide. A model is designed and solved by PO and MOM and the results are identical with measured data.

articleTitle: Effect of the load property on the ESD current
abstract: The effect of the load property on the electrostatic discharge (ESD) current is great. In this paper, the factors affecting the ESD current are analyzed by transmission line theory when the load is linearity. The result indicates that the geometry of the load influences the rise time and the peak value of the ESD current. All the presented results are valuable in researching the electromagnetic interference of the ESD on the EUT.

articleTitle: The Correction of Antenna Factor
abstract: The theoretical NSA values given by the standards are grounded on the assumption that transmit and receive antennas are infinitesimal dipole antennas which is inappropriate to measurements. That is. the assumption neglects: (1) antenna mutual coupling, (2) antenna factor variations versus height, and (3) differences between the H-plane directivities for the measurement antennas and an infinitesimal dipole. Therefore, correction of antenna factor is considered requisite for every NSA measurement, especially when tuned dipoles are employed. In this paper, correction factors are calculated with the method of moments at 3m and Win above a finite metal plane, and the results are compared with that given by ANSI C63.4 and CISPR. To solve the problem of values traceability regarding test site, we give the method below which can take the influence of actual test site into account.

articleTitle: Discussions on Reflection Coefficient's Obtaining Methods in RF Absorber's Simulation
abstract: As the rapid development of the computer technology, full-wave electromagnetic field simulation has been widely used for analyzing and designing RF absorbers' characteristics. In this paper, we discussed on the obtaining methods of the absorber array's reflectivity in HFSS. An error rectifying method was proposed to correct the simulation errors of the incline incidental reflectivity when using a monostatic model.

articleTitle: Preconditioning Matrix for Fast Hierarchical Method in 3-D Capacitance Extraction of IC interconnect
abstract: In 3-D capacitance extraction by indirect boundary element method (BEM), the dense potential coefficient matrix arising from the integral equation formulation is usually represented implicitly and concisely. This is a significant reduction compared to the O(n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) storage that would be required to store potential coefficient matrix directly. Further, the multiplication of matrix-vector product can be accomplished in time proportional to the size of the representation. However, the conventional preconditioning techniques for an explicit matrix are not applicable since no coefficient matrix is actually constructed. In this work, a preconditioning matrix for the fast hierarchical method (FHM) is proposed by carefully examining inherent properties of the hierarchical data structure in the FHM. This preconditioning matrix significantly enhances convergence of the iterative solution yet preserves the implicit nature of the matrix operations in the FHM. Numerical experiments included confirm: this preconditioned FHM reduces iteration times dramatically, and thereby the computational time is reduced.

articleTitle: Analytical Calculation of Impedance of Power/Ground Plane with Circular Holes
abstract: The cavity model method is combined with the extended inverted composition method (ICM) to calculate the impedance of rectangular plane with several circular holes. The agreement of the measured results and the calculated ones validate the presented method. Furthermore, the influence of the holes on the impedance between power and ground plane is discussed.

articleTitle: Analysis of Log-periodic Antenna Array on a Revolving Table
abstract: When a log-periodic antenna array is measured on a three-axis revolving table, because the revolving table is made of metal, it must have some influence on the antenna array' measured results. This paper is to discuss the effect of revolving table on the radiation pattern of antenna array. By using software based on the moment method, the revolving table and the log-periodic antenna array are modeled. And the radiation patterns of the antenna array with and without revolving table are simulated at a few frequencies respectively. The results are compared and a conclusion is reached that the revolving table mainly affects the back lobe, the side lobes and the beam-width of the main lobe, and has little influence on the maximum radiation direction.

articleTitle: Test Site Validation above 1GHz
abstract: It has been proved that the site VSWR is a legitimate validation method to take place of MSA for the frequency above 1GHz. Therefore, the theory of S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">VSWR</sub> and main procedure of testing it are discussed in detail. Finally, considering actual testing environments, we put the sit VSWR into practice and construct a test system by combining the study of software with the structure of hardware, so as to increase efficiency in engineering.

articleTitle: Simulation Study on the Location of a DMB Receiving Antenna in a Portable Multifunction Terminal
abstract: In case of a portable multifunction terminal, the performance of one function can be degraded due to the emitted noise from a PCB trace of another function. In this paper, the electric field intensity around PCB edges emitted from a PCB trace is simulated by changing the location of the trace and allowing the variations of the ground pattern using a commercial electromagnetic solver for a DMB receiver. These results can be used to determine the optimum antenna location having the smallest coupling to the noise. Finally, the several guidelines are proposed for the location of the PCB traces and the receiving antenna.

articleTitle: An Efficient Method for Transmission Line Simulation
abstract: In this paper, a method based SVD (singular value decomposition) was used to cope with singular descript of transmission line model. In order to keep the passivity of the original interconnect model, PRIMA and PRBT were used to reduce the model for fast transmission line simulation.

articleTitle: Implementation of Standing-Traveling Wave Boundary Condition in Homogeneous Isotropic Lossy Media
abstract: Standing-traveling wave boundary condition (STWBC) used in finite-difference time domain (FDTD) simulations is computationally efficient, and is very easy to implement. But the initial implementation was restricted to lossless media. In this paper, STWBC is implemented in homogeneous isotropic lossy media. The perfect electric conducting (PEC) is used in the extension, and the standing wave on the boundary is transformed to the traveling wave. A numerical example is given to validate this implementation.

articleTitle: A Modified Method to Determine the Position to Suspend ADSS Cable on High Voltage Transmission Tower
abstract: In this paper, the method to locate ADSS on power tower is based on MOM. Firstly, possible positions for ADSS cable suspending are obtained based on the IEEE P-1222 standard and distribution of potential around the transmission line and tower. And subsequently, analysis of electric field along the ADSS cable is performed to choose the position where the electric field intensity is lowest as the final location. Considering both the influence of potential and that of the electric field, the discussed technique is effective for the purpose.

articleTitle: Implement of a Set of Microwave Imaging System
abstract: In this paper, a set of microwave imaging system based on SAR (synthetic aperture radar) technology is developed. Wide-band FM CW is applied to realize high rang resolution and SAR technology is used to realize high azimuth resolution. The experimental results show that the design system works well, and 2D image is obtained.

articleTitle: Conversion and Comparison of the Test Results in Fully and Semi-Anechoic Chamber
abstract: This paper illustrates the test method of the radiated emission in Semi-Anechoic Chamber (SAC), and the radiated power in Fully Anechoic Chamber (FAC) between 30MHz and 1GHz. The test results are conversed and compared by analysis, while the correction factors that influence the performance are given.

articleTitle: A Method combining Boundary Integral Equation and Separation Method Applied to Plane Eddy Current Problems
abstract: Eddy currents inside plane conductor of linear permeable material can be excited in two ways: either by an external magnetic field, or by connecting the conductor to a load independent current source. If the excitation is time-harmonic and the frequency is low enough to neglect the displacement current, the modified vector potential describing the fields of the given plane eddy current problem is governed by a Helmholtz' equation. This equation can be solved by separation. The solution is inserted into the remaining boundary integral equation for the exterior vector potential in the domain surrounding the conductor yielding a system of linear equations. This method has been applied to a rectangular conductor. Numerical results will be given and compared with the results of commercial simulation software.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Field Distribution inside Dielectric Object Loaded in TEM Cell Using Hybrid FEM-BEM Method
abstract: The field distribution inside the dielectric equipment under test (EUT) loaded in transverse electromagnetic (TEM) cell is researched. The FEM-BEM domain decomposition method was proposed. For the EUT, which is the interested region, the finite element method was applied, while for the TEM cell the boundary element method is used. This method reduces the computational time and memory requirement. The results obtained by the hybrid FEM-BEM method are compared with those obtained by other methods. The present method is an efficient technique, which can be widely used for the analysis of field distribution inside the complicated dielectric EUT surrounded by large or infinite electromagnetic field.

articleTitle: EMC Design in Signal-Generating Circuit of Electromagnetic Position System
abstract: According to the theory of electromagnetic position system, a sine signal-generating circuit is designed. In the design of PCB, RF emission of IC and EMI of PCB has been analyzed. The EMC rules of component choice, component placement, trace wiring and grounding is presented. Some EMC simulated results of the circuit by HyperLynx software is given in the end.

articleTitle: A Novel Method to Calculate Electric Field Distribution and Characteristic Impedance In ATEM Cell with Rectangular Metallic EUT
abstract: ATEM cell is widely used in electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) test. When loaded with equipment under test (EUT), the electric field in ATEM cell will be distorted , and the characteristic impedance changed. In this paper, the field distribution and characteristic impedance in ATEM cell loaded with rectangular metallic EUT is analyzed by a simple method---point matching method. The section of an asymmetric TEM was divided into five regions and potential function is expressed as a Fourier series in each region. The point-matching was used on the interface of these regions to determine coefficients of series. Thus, the characteristic impedance can be calculated and electric field obtained in terms of a potential function.

articleTitle: Some EMC Problems Possibly Faced By the Next-Generation Network
abstract: The NGN characteristics are described, and its main EMC problems are analyzed. The article focuses on discussions on the spectrum utilization efficiency and dynamic spectrum access, and the management of divers heterogeneous access networks.

articleTitle: Influence of Parameters of the Transient Grounding Model on Numerical Analysis and Experimental Verification
abstract: This paper discussed the influence of the parameters of the transient grounding model on numerical analysis using FDTD method; some useful results are given and verified by the experiment.

articleTitle: Power Line Communication Applications within UMTS Scenarios
abstract: The idea of the PLC integration with UMTS is to achieve the connection of UMTS entities through PLC links. PLC can be very interesting in particular in Micro-Node B scenarios. Another application is to use -vice versa-UMTS as PLC backhaul. Integrated subscription for UMTS and PLC services appears also as a very interesting business models in areas where PLC is commercially rolled-out.

articleTitle: Effects of Exposure to EMP on the morphology in the main organs of rats
abstract: To investigate the effects of electromagnetic pulse (EMP) on the morphology of the rat's main organs (lung, kidney, liver, spleen, heart, testicle, ovary, and so on). Light microscope was used to observe the pathological changes in the main organs after the rats were exposed to EMP with respectively 1000, 1100 and 12000 pulses at different time point. After 24 hours exposure to 1000 and 1100 pulses of EMP, the alveolus epithelium were lightly swoln, dilatation and congestion were found in the blood vessel of the alveolar wall and the glomerulus. After 3 days exposure, the morphostructure of alveolus, glomerulus and the renal tubule got right. There were no significant changes in other organs yet. Shortly after the 12000 pulses exposure and till 24 hours, congestion and swelling became more serious in the lung and the glomerulus with haemorrhage and eosinophils infiltration. The sacculus expanded evidently with a large amount of tubular protein casts. Congestions were also found in the liver, cardiac muscle, testicle, ovary, spleen and wall of digestive tract. The lesion aggravated gradually with dosages increasing. All these changes returned to normal after 3 days exposure. Results suggested that exposure to EMP of 12000 pulses would obviously increase the permeability of the blood vessel, especially in the organs with function of blood exchange barrier such as the glomerular filtration barrier or the air-blood barrier in alveolar wall.

articleTitle: Limits of Discharge parameters in Short-gap Human-metal ESD at Special Charge Voltage
abstract: Discharge parameters, affected by electrode approach speed, appear their limits for charge voltage V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> =800 V in electrostatic discharge through a handheld-approaching-small rod from charged human body, which reveal the transition to avalanche from surface emission in short-gap ESD. Discharge process is dominated by avalanche phase for V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> = 800 V, which produce discharge current with blunt peak. Discharge parameters extreme values, analyzed with electric circuit theory, are results from mutual action of distributive capacitance and channel resistance across the gap during approach of the electrodes. Mutual action of distributive capacitance and non-linear channel resistance is the dominative cause for the existence of extreme values at special charge voltage V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> = 800 V. Circuit theory has been employed to elucidate the threshold phenomenon.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Shielding Effectiveness of Rectangular Concrete Enclosure
abstract: Based on the Method of Moment and the volume integral equation, a general technique for analyzing the electromagnetic shielding properties of rectangular concrete enclosures is presented. After deriving the volume integral equation for the internal electric field, we proceeded to solve the equation numerically by MOM. The comparison between the calculation results of this paper and calculation results of other paper shows that the method is effective. The approach can be used to analyze the shielding effectiveness of protection cell in substation, and the shielding effectiveness of a concrete protection cell model is calculated in this paper.

articleTitle: Calculation of the Induced Current of a Shielded Inner Conductor Coupled by an EMP Field
abstract: The proposed DF-FDTD method can be used to build a model for the transfer impedance. According to this transfer impedance model and the induced current of the outer conductor, the induced current and voltage of the inner conductor can be obtained by the transmission line (TL) model. This work can provide the theory support for the protection of the inner conductor from the EMP field.

articleTitle: Changes of microwave radiation on the level of trace elements in mice bone tissues
abstract: To investigate effects of microwave radiation on levels of microelement in bone tissues of mice. Microwave with a frequency of 2450MHz and a power density of 10mW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> was used. Variation of levels of microelements and effect of drugs were observed. And thereby bioeffects of microwave on mice were studied. In microwave group bone tissues contents of microelements Ca and Zn dropped significantly (p≪0.01), and Cu, Fe and Mn presented a trend of decrease compared with normal. Following radiation, in comparison with microwave group, LBD group presented a rise in contents of Ca and Zn in bone tissues, approaching normal levels. Conclusion: Microwave radiation can result in decrease in contents of microelements Ca and Zn in bone tissues, and LBD was of resistance against microwave radiation.

articleTitle: A 40GHz Amplifier Design Using CPW
abstract: In this paper, a 40 GHz amplifier is realized with its matching network and inductors realized with CPW.
